+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from collections.abc import Iterable
+from os import PathLike
+
+from _pytest.pathlib import absolutepath
+from _pytest.pathlib import module_name_from_path
+
+
+def module_inventory(
+    paths: Iterable[str | PathLike[str]], root: str | PathLike[str]
+) -> list[str]:
+    """Return unique dotted module labels in the order they first appear.
+
+    Relative paths are interpreted from the current working directory. No files
+    need to exist.
+    """
+    root_path = absolutepath(root)
+    labels = (module_name_from_path(absolutepath(path), root_path) for path in paths)
+    return list(dict.fromkeys(labels))

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from _pytest.module_inventory import module_inventory
+import pytest
+
+
+def test_module_inventory_preserves_first_seen_labels(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    root = tmp_path / "project"
+    paths = [
+        root / "z.py",
+        str(root / ".pkg" / "a.b.py"),
+        root / "pkg" / "__init__.py",
+        root / "z.py",
+        root / "_pkg" / "a_b.py",
+        root / "pkg.py",
+        root / "__init__.py",
+        root / "script",
+    ]
+
+    assert module_inventory(iter(paths), str(root)) == [
+        "z",
+        "_pkg.a_b",
+        "pkg",
+        "__init__",
+        "script",
+    ]
+
+
+def test_module_inventory_outside_root(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    root = tmp_path / "project"
+    package = tmp_path / "project.other"
+    label = ".".join(part.replace(".", "_") for part in package.parts[1:])
+
+    assert module_inventory([package / "__init__.py"], root) == [label]
+
+
+def test_module_inventory_relative_paths(
+    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
+) -> None:
+    monkeypatch.chdir(tmp_path)
+    paths = ["project/pkg/../mod.py", tmp_path / "project" / "mod.py"]
+
+    assert module_inventory(paths, Path("project")) == ["mod"]
+
+
+def test_module_inventory_empty(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
+    assert module_inventory([], tmp_path) == []
notes:
The implementation normalizes paths without checking the filesystem, then reuses pytest's existing module-name formatter and deduplicates the resulting labels in first-seen order.
